items.title: 33.4 Water Pollution due to Human Activities

source_refs.note: Topic 33.4 with Quick Check 33.4 (PDF 254-255). Quick Check answers were derived for the lesson and need review.

blocks.text: Human activities are a major cause of water pollution across the globe. As populations grow and industries expand, more waste and pollutants enter water bodies, and improper waste management and weak environmental regulation often let contaminants reach rivers, lakes and oceans.

items: Industrial activities: the major source of water pollution. Factories often discharge harmful chemicals, heavy metals and toxic waste directly into rivers, lakes and oceans; common polluting industries include oil refineries, chemical plants, the automobile industry, fertiliser plants and tanneries.

Agricultural activities: runoff carries fertilisers, pesticides and herbicides into nearby water. Poor irrigation increases soil erosion, washing sediment into rivers and streams, and farm drainage contaminates both surface water and groundwater.

Domestic and municipal waste: untreated or poorly treated sewage and solid waste from cities are often discharged directly into rivers, lakes or oceans, adding harmful bacteria and viruses. Household detergents, oils and chemicals enter drains and reach water bodies, and plastics dumped in or near channels cause blockages and long-term pollution.

Deforestation and land use for urban development: when trees and vegetation are removed, loose soil erodes and more sediment enters rivers, clogging waterways and harming habitats; construction adds pollutants and debris to runoff.
Recreational activities: boating, swimming and camping can pollute water if not managed; boats release oil, fuel and chemicals, and visitors drop plastics, food wrappers and other litter.

Marine transport: ships and boats discharge oil, fuel and other chemicals; accidental oil spills, wastewater and sewage from vessels, and routine maintenance such as hull cleaning and painting release toxic substances.

blocks.text: A river passes three regions: a rural area with large farms and many cattle; an industrial area with many paint and battery industries; and a large residential area of a big city.

items: (i) Which type of pollutants, organic, inorganic or both, will the rural area add? Name two. (ii) Which metals are most likely near the industrial area?
(iii) Which regions will add chemicals that lead to eutrophication? (iv) Name four contaminants from the residential area.
